one_liner: Node.js addon running the uWebSockets C++ server behind JS callbacks; 2.6x Fastify, about 1.06x actix-web on hello-world.
what_it_does: Serves HTTP/1.1, WebSockets and experimental HTTP/3 from a native V8 addon instead of node:http. uWS.App()/SSLApp()/H3App() register routes as (res, req) callbacks, and WebSocket behaviors are plain objects with open/message/drain/close handlers plus built-in topic pub/sub. The API is its own, not Express- or node:http-compatible: HttpRequest is stack-allocated and dies when the handler returns or awaits, HttpResponse dies on end() or abort, and request bodies arrive as chunked ArrayBuffers through onData/onDataV2/collectBody.
how_it_is_fast: HTTP parsing, routing, TLS (BoringSSL), WebSocket framing and compression run in the uWebSockets C++ core, driven by Node's own libuv loop (built with LIBUS_USE_LIBUV, attached via node::GetCurrentEventLoop) and compiled with clang -O3 -flto. The binding keeps its own overhead small: req/res are clones of pre-built V8 object templates holding a raw pointer, incoming data arrives as zero-copy ArrayBuffers detached after the callback, and the synchronous part of each handler runs corked so its writes leave in one syscall. Two paths skip JS entirely: DeclarativeResponse compiles a response into opcodes that C++ replays per request, and v20.71.0 added experimental per-route microcaching with coalesced refreshes. What the binding costs is the C++-to-JS crossing: every handler call goes through node::MakeCallback, which the maintainer names as the main bottleneck (issues #1209, #1288).
when_to_use: Node.js 22/24/26 services that must stay on Node and are bound by HTTP or WebSocket I/O: in the same 2026-09-24 run it did 174,621 req/s at c=512 against 68,128 for Fastify and 42,586 for Express on the same 4 cores.

WebSocket fan-out such as chat, game or market-data servers that need pub/sub, per-socket backpressure limits (maxBackpressure, closeOnBackpressureLimit, drain) and permessage-deflate options without extra packages.

Hot endpoints with static or templated answers (DeclarativeResponse), or idempotent 'dynamic but public' GET endpoints that tolerate brief staleness (experimental microcache; wired only for non-TLS App GET routes, expiry units not documented).
Teams that accept a low-level, callback-first API and will put their own routing and middleware conventions on top.
when_not_to_use: C++ programs: use the uWebSockets core directly. This repository adds only the V8 glue (src/addon.cpp and the *Wrapper.h files) on top of it.

Apps that need the Express/Connect middleware ecosystem, a fetch-style Request that survives await, or streams-based node:http compatibility. Ultimate Express or fulmine.js give that API on the same core.

Bun users or peak-JS-throughput chasers: the maintainer says Bun (built on a uWS fork) now beats this addon 'by a wide margin' on WebSocket echo, because every C++-to-JS call must go through node::MakeCallback (issue #1288).
Alpine/musl, Deno, Node versions other than 22/24/26, or 32-bit targets: only prebuilt glibc Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64 and Windows x64 binaries exist, one per Node ABI (127/137/147).

Organisations that require npm-registry packages, provenance, or a plain OSS licence: it installs from GitHub tags only, and the README says 'all rights reserved' except where an Apache-2.0 notice is given.

integration.form: module (prebuilt native .node addon plus uws.js loader, installed with npm from a GitHub tag; not on the npm registry)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; the prebuilt binary statically bundles the uWebSockets/uSockets core, BoringSSL and lsquic (HTTP/3)
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 22, 24 or 26 (v8 ABI 127/137/147); rebuilding from source needs clang-18 on Linux (clang on macOS/Windows), CMake, and C++20
integration.platforms: glibc Linux x86-64 and aarch64, macOS x86-64 and arm64 (macOS 12 target), Windows x86-64; not musl
integration.thread_safety: Each Node worker thread or cluster process creates its own App on its own event loop. Multi-core scaling uses SO_REUSEPORT listening (Linux) or an acceptor App that round-robins sockets to child apps via addChildAppDescriptor. Sharing App/res/ws objects across threads is not documented. The built-in KV store (getString/setString and friends) is process-global and guarded only by explicit lock()/unlock().

gotchas: A handler that returns without responding and without calling res.onAborted() makes the C++ core call std::terminate(); the process dies and process.on('uncaughtException') never fires (issue #1296). ASAN builds in the binaries-asan branch help locate such crashes.

req is unusable after the first await or after the handler returns, and res is unusable after end() or abort; both throw. onData/onDataV2 chunks and WebSocket message ArrayBuffers are detached after the callback, so copy them if you keep them.
Writes made after an await or from timers/DB callbacks must be wrapped in res.cork(); otherwise the addon prints a warning on each write and loses the one-syscall batching.

Performance tweaks have regressed before: v20.62.0 disabled the WebSocket.send V8 fast call after reports of broken apps, and the v20.63.0 string fast path sent Latin-1 bytes instead of UTF-8 until v20.65.0 reverted it. The ESM wrapper is hard-coded (open issue #1314), and the benchmark suite loaded 20.71.0 through CommonJS to avoid it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick the raw binding over Ultimate Express or fulmine.js (Express-compatible layers on the same core) when you write to uWS's own API and need its WebSocket pub/sub and backpressure control; it is not automatically faster, since fulmine.js, which answers simple handlers without running JS, scored 203,996 req/s against this binding's 174,621 at c=512 in the same run. If you can leave Node, Elysia on Bun (173,877 req/s) runs a uWS fork without the MakeCallback toll.
verified_claims_summary: In the-benchmarker/web-frameworks run of 2026-09-24 (zrk closed loop, hello-world GET/GET-param/POST routes averaged, server pinned to 4 cores of an undisclosed 16-thread x86-64 Linux host), uWebSockets.js v20.71.0 on Node 26 as a one-worker-per-core cluster with plain JS callbacks did 189,157 / 178,265 / 174,621 req/s at c=64/256/512 against 179,203 / 168,270 / 163,415 for actix-web 4.8 (Rust 1.98, LTO, codegen-units=1), 1.06-1.07x. Other snapshots gave 0.99-1.04x and 1.33-1.42x, so read it as parity with actix and roughly 2.6x Fastify and 4.1x Express in the same run; the README's '13x faster than Fastify' compares the author's microcached endpoint with an uncached Fastify hello-world.
status_note: Actively maintained by its original author (uWS dates from 2016, this binding from 2018; v20.71.0 released 2026-09-16, last push 2026-09-20). It ships only as GitHub-hosted prebuilt binaries tied to three Node majors, under an 'all rights reserved, Apache-2.0 where noticed' licence statement, and the maintainer has said the Node binding will eventually 'fade into the background' in favour of Bun.
